proofs.full_local_argument: Local reconstruction, not a quotation or claim that the source prints this full proof. Write h_k=||b_k||_2^2. At k=0, alpha_0=(Ab_0)^T b_0/h_0 makes b_1 orthogonal to b_0. Suppose b_0,...,b_k are nonzero and mutually orthogonal. The specified alpha_k directly gives b_{k+1}^T b_k=0; for k>=1 the specified beta_{k-1} gives b_{k+1}^T b_{k-1}=0, since the previous vectors are orthogonal. For 0<=j<=k-2, symmetry and the earlier recurrence give b_j^T Ab_k=(Ab_j)^T b_k=0: Ab_j=b_{j+1}+alpha_j b_j+beta_{j-1}b_{j-1}, with the last term omitted at j=0, and every vector on the right has index <=k-1. The correction terms also have zero dot product with b_j. Thus b_{k+1} is orthogonal to every previous vector, and induction applies until it is zero. For k>=1, symmetry gives b_{k-1}^T Ab_k=(Ab_{k-1})^T b_k=h_k, so beta_{k-1}=h_k/h_{k-1}>0. Every b_k is a monic polynomial of degree k in A applied to b_0: this holds at k=0 and follows at each subsequent step because multiplication by A contributes the unique leading term. Therefore b_0,...,b_{n-1} and b_0,Ab_0,...,A^{n-1}b_0 have the same span by a triangular change of generators with unit diagonal. If b_1,...,b_{d-1} are all nonzero, the d orthogonal vectors b_0,...,b_{d-1} span R^d; b_d is orthogonal to that space and is zero. Hence the first zero index exists with 1<=m<=d. At that index every Ab_j for j<m is a linear combination of b_0,...,b_{m-1}, including j=m-1 because b_m=0. This proves invariance. Normalize q_j=b_j/sqrt(h_j). For j<m-1, the recurrence becomes Aq_j=(sqrt(h_{j+1})/sqrt(h_j))q_{j+1}+alpha_j q_j+(sqrt(h_j)/sqrt(h_{j-1}))q_{j-1}, omitting the previous term at j=0. For j=m-1 the next-vector term is zero. These column identities give the stated T_n and residual relation for all n<=m. Since Q_n has orthonormal columns and b_n is orthogonal to them or zero, multiplication on the left by Q_n^T gives Q_n^T A Q_n=T_n. Finally, if Av=lambda v and v^T b_0=0, symmetry gives v^T A^j b_0=lambda^j v^T b_0=0 for every j>=0. Such an eigenvector is orthogonal to every generated vector. No recovery outside the cyclic subspace follows.

assumptions: A is a real d by d symmetric matrix and b_0 is a nonzero vector in R^d.
All products and arithmetic are exact. Stop at the first zero residual before division by its norm.
statement.conclusion: The nonzero vectors b_0,...,b_{m-1} are mutually orthogonal. For every n<=m their first n vectors span K_n(A,b_0). For 1<=k<m, beta_{k-1}=||b_k||_2^2/||b_{k-1}||_2^2. Q_n^T A Q_n=T_n and A Q_n=Q_n T_n+(b_n/||b_{n-1}||_2)e_n^T, where e_n is the last coordinate vector in R^n and the residual term is zero for n=m. K_m is A-invariant. Any eigenvector v of A with v^T b_0=0 is orthogonal to every generated vector; recovery outside the cyclic subspace is not guaranteed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the Euclidean inner product on R^d. Set b_{-1}=0 and beta_{-1}=0. Whenever b_k!=0, let w_k=Ab_k and alpha_k=w_k^T b_k/||b_k||_2^2. For k>=1 let beta_{k-1}=w_k^T b_{k-1}/||b_{k-1}||_2^2. Set b_{k+1}=w_k-alpha_k b_k-beta_{k-1}b_{k-1}, omitting the last term at k=0. Let m be the first index >=1 with b_m=0. Define K_n(A,b_0)=span{b_0,Ab_0,...,A^{n-1}b_0}, q_j=b_j/||b_j||_2 for j<m, and Q_n=[q_0,...,q_{n-1}]. Define T_n to have diagonal alpha_0,...,alpha_{n-1} and symmetric off-diagonals (T_n)_{i,i+1}=(T_n)_{i+1,i}=||b_i||_2/||b_{i-1}||_2 for 1<=i<n, using 1-based matrix indices.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=1 integer; the first breakdown index exists with 1<=m<=d; n is an integer in [1,m]. No accuracy parameter, spectral gap, positive definiteness or random initialization is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer d>=1 and every such A and b_0, the deterministic recurrence has the stated properties for every integer n with 1<=n<=m.
